prompt: A security reviewer reading packages/delegation is alarmed that anyone with write access can store new versions of a company's Role and Delegation records in its eVault. They ask three things: why the eVault does not refuse those writes, why a verifier stops reading a record's history after 2,000 versions, and why a Company record whose first version had no directors can never get a board, even when a later version adds directors and is signed by one of them. What is the answer to each?
key: Written in docs/docs/W3DS Protocol/Company-Delegation.md (the opening, "Company: born with its board" and "Limits and trade-offs"); the code is packages/delegation (history.ts resolveBoard / board timeline, chain.ts) and packages/auth/src/delegated-signature.ts (HISTORY_PAGE 100 x MAX_HISTORY_PAGES 20). (1) The eVault enforces none of the delegation model: it stores whatever it is given, and all authority is decided by the verifier from signatures and the eVault's version history. Writes are not restricted; records that are not properly signed (unsigned, forged, copied or written back) are ignored as if absent, so they cost verification time but grant nothing. (2) Because anyone can add versions, the read is bounded: a verifier reads at most 2,000 versions of a record, so flooding a record with writes is a denial of service, never a takeover. (3) A board only counts if the Company record's very first version already carries one signed by one of its own directors; after that only a sitting director may change it. A record that started without directors can never acquire a board, so an existing company cannot be claimed by whoever adds directors first.

**History size:** a verifier reads at most 2,000 versions of any one record. Flooding a record with writes is a denial of service, never a takeover.

A board only counts if the Company record's **very first version** already carries one, signed by one of its own directors. A Company record that started without directors can never acquire a board, so an existing company cannot be claimed by whoever adds directors first.
